outline: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Loading conditions and systolic anterior motion
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with dynamic LV outflow tract obstruction
mechanism: In obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, asymmetric septal hypertrophy and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve create a dynamic LV outflow tract gradient. Reduced preload or afterload and increased contractility shrink the LV cavity and worsen obstruction, so the murmur intensifies with standing or Valsalva and decreases with squatting or increased afterload.
vignette: A 21-year-old man has exertional presyncope. His father died suddenly at age 38. Cardiac examination shows a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at the left sternal border that becomes louder when he stands from a squatting position and softer when he squats. Echocardiography shows marked asymmetric basal septal hypertrophy.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractors: Valvular aortic stenosis
Atrial septal defect
Mitral valve prolapse
Dilated cardiomyopathy
distractor_notes: Aortic stenosis produces a fixed valvular obstruction whose murmur generally does not increase with reduced preload in the characteristic manner described; the young age, family history, and asymmetric septal hypertrophy favor HCM.
An atrial septal defect classically produces a fixed split S2 and a flow murmur rather than a preload-sensitive dynamic outflow murmur with asymmetric septal hypertrophy.

Mitral valve prolapse can become more prominent with reduced LV volume, but echocardiographic asymmetric septal hypertrophy and a harsh LVOT-type murmur point to obstructive HCM rather than isolated leaflet prolapse.
Dilated cardiomyopathy produces ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction rather than asymmetric septal hypertrophy with dynamic LV outflow obstruction.
key_expl: Obstructive HCM is characterized by asymmetric septal hypertrophy and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. The LVOT gradient is dynamic and worsens when preload or afterload falls, explaining the louder murmur with standing and softer murmur with squatting.
objective: Recognize obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from family history, asymmetric septal hypertrophy, and a systolic murmur that increases when preload falls.
clues: murmur louder standing and softer squatting

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Adenosine-mediated tubuloglomerular feedback after increased macula densa sodium chloride delivery
mechanism: When NaCl delivery to the macula densa increases, NKCC2-dependent sensing promotes ATP release and extracellular adenosine generation. Adenosine activates A1 receptors on afferent arteriolar smooth muscle, increasing vascular resistance and lowering single-nephron GFR.
vignette: In an isolated nephron preparation, sodium chloride delivery to the macula densa is abruptly increased while systemic arterial pressure remains constant. The same nephron subsequently shows a decrease in glomerular filtration rate.
lead: Which local response most directly mediates this change?
correct: Adenosine A1 receptor-mediated constriction of the afferent arteriole
distractors: Nitric oxide-mediated dilation of the afferent arteriole
Angiotensin II-mediated dilation of the efferent arteriole
Prostaglandin E2-mediated dilation of the afferent arteriole
Atrial natriuretic peptide-mediated constriction of the afferent arteriole
distractor_notes: Nitric oxide tends to blunt tubuloglomerular feedback by opposing vasoconstriction rather than serving as the principal mediator of the fall in GFR after increased macula densa NaCl.
Angiotensin II preferentially constricts rather than dilates the efferent arteriole and acts as a modulator/cofactor rather than the local A1-mediated effector specified here.
PGE2 can promote renin release and vasodilation; the constrictor response to high macula densa NaCl is mediated principally by ATP-derived adenosine acting on A1 receptors.
ANP generally promotes natriuresis and increases glomerular filtration through effects that do not correspond to the local macula-densa A1 feedback pathway.
key_expl: Tubuloglomerular feedback is a nephron-specific negative-feedback loop. High macula densa NaCl increases ATP/adenosine signaling; adenosine activates A1 receptors on afferent arteriolar smooth muscle, causing vasoconstriction and reducing GFR.
objective: Explain how increased macula densa sodium chloride delivery lowers GFR through adenosine A1 receptor-mediated afferent arteriolar constriction.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Acid in the duodenum stimulates S cells to release secretin. Secretin activates basolateral Gs-coupled receptors on pancreatic ductal/centroacinar cells, increasing cAMP and promoting bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion. Apical CFTR is central to ductal chloride/bicarbonate transport and supports highly alkaline pancreatic juice.
vignette: Acidic gastric contents enter the duodenum after a meal. A hormone released from duodenal S cells raises cAMP in pancreatic ductal cells, producing a large volume of bicarbonate-rich pancreatic fluid.
lead: Which apical membrane protein is most important for this ductal response?
distractors: Na+-glucose cotransporter 1
H+/K+-ATPase
Epithelial sodium channel
Niemann-Pick C1-like 1 transporter
distractor_notes: SGLT1 mediates intestinal glucose and galactose uptake and is not the principal apical anion channel supporting pancreatic ductal bicarbonate secretion.
The H+/K+-ATPase is the gastric parietal-cell proton pump and does not mediate pancreatic duct bicarbonate secretion.
ENaC is important in distal epithelial sodium absorption and does not drive the secretin-stimulated pancreatic ductal bicarbonate response.
NPC1L1 mediates intestinal sterol uptake and is unrelated to pancreatic ductal bicarbonate transport.
key_expl: Secretin raises cAMP in pancreatic duct cells and stimulates bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion. CFTR at the apical membrane is a central regulator and conduit for chloride/bicarbonate transport required for normal pancreatic duct secretion.
objective: Connect secretin-induced pancreatic bicarbonate secretion to cAMP-dependent activation of apical CFTR in ductal cells.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Escape from the Wolff-Chaikoff effect through reduced thyroidal iodide uptake
mechanism: A large iodide load acutely suppresses thyroid hormone synthesis (Wolff-Chaikoff effect). After several days, normal thyroid tissue escapes by decreasing sodium-iodide symporter expression/activity, lowering intrathyroidal iodide below the inhibitory threshold and allowing organification and hormone synthesis to resume.
vignette: A euthyroid adult receives a sustained large iodide load. Thyroid hormone synthesis falls transiently but returns toward baseline several days later despite continued high plasma iodide concentrations.
lead: Which cellular adaptation most directly permits this recovery?
correct: Downregulation of the basolateral sodium-iodide symporter
distractors: Upregulation of thyroid peroxidase-mediated iodide organification during the initial inhibitory phase
Increased expression of the TSH receptor despite persistently suppressed iodide uptake
Increased apical pendrin-mediated iodide transport into the follicular lumen as the primary escape mechanism
Inhibition of thyroglobulin endocytosis from the follicular lumen
distractor_notes: The acute Wolff-Chaikoff state suppresses organification; recovery occurs by reducing intrathyroidal iodide rather than by simply increasing TPO activity against the same excess iodide load.
TSH-receptor expression is not the principal mechanism of escape from acute iodide-induced inhibition.
Pendrin participates in apical iodide transport, but the established escape mechanism centers on reduced NIS-mediated iodide uptake and lower intracellular iodide.
Blocking thyroglobulin endocytosis would reduce thyroid hormone release rather than restore hormone synthesis.
key_expl: Normal thyroid tissue escapes the Wolff-Chaikoff effect by reducing NIS expression/activity. Lower iodide influx decreases intrathyroidal iodide concentration below the level that suppresses organification, permitting thyroid hormone synthesis to resume.
objective: Explain escape from the Wolff-Chaikoff effect as downregulation of the thyroid sodium-iodide symporter and reduction of intrathyroidal iodide.
clues: transient fall in thyroid hormone synthesis
recovery despite continued high plasma iodide

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Loss of cochlear amplification from impaired outer hair cell prestin
mechanism: Outer hair cells change length in response to membrane-potential changes through the motor protein prestin in their lateral membrane. This electromotility feeds mechanical energy back into the cochlea, amplifying basilar-membrane motion and sharpening auditory sensitivity and frequency selectivity.
vignette: An experimental mutation selectively abolishes electromotility of cochlear outer hair cells while preserving their mechanoelectrical transduction channels and leaving inner hair cells structurally intact. Auditory thresholds rise markedly.
lead: Loss of which protein most directly explains this finding?
distractors: Connexin 43
Myosin II in middle-ear ossicular muscles
Synaptotagmin in inner hair cell ribbon synapses
Aquaporin-4 in supporting cells
distractor_notes: Connexins participate in gap-junction networks in the cochlea, but the voltage-driven somatic electromotility of outer hair cells specifically depends on prestin.
Middle-ear muscle contractile proteins do not generate the active cochlear amplifier within outer hair cells.
Inner hair cell synaptic release is essential for afferent transmission, but the stem preserves inner hair cells and selectively removes outer-hair-cell electromotility.
Aquaporin-mediated water transport is not the molecular motor responsible for rapid outer-hair-cell length changes.
key_expl: Prestin is the lateral-membrane motor protein of outer hair cells. Voltage-dependent conformational changes in prestin drive outer-hair-cell electromotility, which is essential for the mammalian cochlear amplifier and normal hearing sensitivity.
objective: Identify prestin as the molecular motor responsible for outer hair cell electromotility and cochlear amplification.

outline: Carbonic anhydrase II and vacuolar H+-ATPase
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Osteoclast-mediated bone resorption through acidification of the resorption lacuna
mechanism: Activated osteoclasts form a sealed resorption lacuna beneath the ruffled border. Carbonic anhydrase II generates intracellular H+ and bicarbonate; vacuolar H+-ATPases pump H+ across the ruffled border, while chloride transport maintains electroneutrality. Acid dissolves hydroxyapatite, allowing proteases to degrade organic matrix.
vignette: A child has increased bone density due to an inherited osteoclast defect. Osteoclast number is normal, but the cells cannot acidify the compartment between the ruffled border and the bone surface.
lead: Failure of which transport process most directly impairs mineral dissolution?
correct: Vacuolar H+-ATPase-mediated proton secretion across the ruffled border
distractors: Na+/K+-ATPase-mediated sodium extrusion across the basolateral membrane
CFTR-mediated bicarbonate secretion into the resorption lacuna
ENaC-mediated sodium entry across the ruffled border
SGLT2-mediated glucose uptake across the ruffled border
distractor_notes: Na+/K+-ATPase supports general cellular ion gradients but does not directly acidify the osteoclast resorption lacuna.
Bicarbonate secretion into the lacuna would buffer acid rather than generate the low pH needed to dissolve hydroxyapatite.
ENaC is not the principal acidifying transporter of the osteoclast ruffled border.
SGLT2 is a renal proximal-tubule glucose transporter and does not mediate osteoclastic mineral dissolution.
key_expl: Osteoclasts dissolve bone mineral by pumping protons into the sealed resorption lacuna through vacuolar H+-ATPases in the ruffled border. Carbonic anhydrase II supplies protons, and chloride transport preserves electroneutrality.
objective: Explain osteoclast bone resorption by linking ruffled-border vacuolar H+-ATPase activity to acidification and hydroxyapatite dissolution.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Congenital methemoglobinemia due to cytochrome b5 reductase deficiency
mechanism: Cytochrome b5 reductase (NADH-dependent methemoglobin reductase) normally reduces ferric Fe3+ heme iron back to ferrous Fe2+ using reducing equivalents derived from glycolytic NADH. Autosomal-recessive deficiency causes persistent methemoglobinemia and cyanosis despite normal arterial oxygen tension.
vignette: A 17-year-old boy has had slate-gray cyanosis since childhood but normal exercise tolerance. His parents are first cousins and are asymptomatic. Arterial blood gas shows a normal PaO2, whereas pulse oximetry remains approximately 85%. Blood is chocolate-brown, and methemoglobin is persistently elevated in the absence of oxidant-drug exposure.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractors: Hemoglobin M disease
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency
Carbon monoxide poisoning
Sulfhemoglobinemia from sulfonamide exposure
distractor_notes: Hemoglobin M can cause congenital methemoglobinemia but is typically autosomal dominant; the consanguineous unaffected-parent pedigree favors autosomal-recessive cytochrome b5 reductase deficiency.
G6PD deficiency predisposes to oxidant hemolysis and can complicate methylene-blue treatment but is not the normal primary methemoglobin-reduction defect causing lifelong isolated cyanosis.
Carbon monoxide poisoning produces carboxyhemoglobinemia and exposure-related tissue hypoxia, not lifelong chocolate-brown blood with elevated methemoglobin.
Sulfhemoglobinemia is acquired after exposure to certain sulfur-containing drugs and is not consistent with lifelong cyanosis in the absence of exposure.
key_expl: Cytochrome b5 reductase is the major physiologic pathway that keeps methemoglobin below 1% by reducing Fe3+ heme iron to Fe2+ using NADH. Autosomal-recessive deficiency produces congenital methemoglobinemia with cyanosis, saturation gap, and normal PaO2.
objective: Recognize congenital cytochrome b5 reductase deficiency from lifelong cyanosis, elevated methemoglobin, normal PaO2, and an autosomal-recessive pedigree.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: PERK-mediated translational attenuation during the unfolded protein response
mechanism: Accumulation of unfolded proteins in the ER activates PERK, an ER transmembrane kinase. Activated PERK phosphorylates eIF2α at Ser51, which inhibits eIF2B-mediated nucleotide exchange and decreases formation of the translation-initiation ternary complex, transiently reducing global protein synthesis and ER folding load.
vignette: A secretory cell is exposed to a drug that causes accumulation of misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum. Within minutes, global translation initiation falls before transcriptional remodeling of the secretory pathway is complete.
lead: Which signaling event most directly causes this early reduction in protein synthesis?
distractors: IRE1-mediated splicing of XBP1 mRNA
ATF6 cleavage in the Golgi apparatus
mTORC1-mediated phosphorylation of S6 kinase
Ubiquitination of all cytosolic ribosomal proteins
distractor_notes: IRE1-XBP1 signaling increases ER folding and secretory capacity through transcriptional programs but is not the principal immediate mechanism of global translation attenuation.
ATF6 cleavage generates a transcription factor that increases ER homeostatic gene expression; it does not directly produce the rapid global translational block.
mTORC1 activation generally promotes translation rather than mediating the PERK-dependent reduction in protein synthesis during ER stress.
The early UPR does not require wholesale ubiquitination and destruction of ribosomes; it transiently attenuates initiation through eIF2α phosphorylation.
key_expl: PERK is one of the three canonical ER-stress sensors. It phosphorylates eIF2α, inhibiting eIF2B-dependent recycling and reducing global translation initiation, which decreases the influx of newly synthesized proteins into the stressed ER.
objective: Identify PERK-mediated eIF2α phosphorylation as the rapid translational-attenuation arm of the unfolded protein response.

diagnosis: Collider bias from conditioning on a common effect
mechanism: A collider is a variable caused by two other variables. Conditioning on, stratifying by, or restricting a sample according to the collider can create a noncausal association between its causes even when they are otherwise independent. This is a form of selection bias and can distort causal estimates.
vignette: Investigators study whether chronic opioid use is associated with severe postoperative pain. Both chronic opioid use and severe postoperative pain independently increase the probability that a patient will be referred to a specialty pain clinic. The investigators include only patients seen in that clinic and observe an inverse association between opioid use and severe pain.
lead: Which bias most directly threatens this study?
correct: Collider bias from conditioning on specialty-clinic referral
distractors: Recall bias
Lead-time bias
Nonresponse bias
Regression to the mean
distractor_notes: Recall bias requires systematic differences in the accuracy of remembered exposures or outcomes; the problem here is selection on a common effect of exposure and outcome.
Lead-time bias concerns earlier diagnosis through screening and apparent survival extension without changed mortality; no screening-survival framework is present.
Nonresponse bias concerns differential participation or survey response; the described distortion arises specifically because referral is caused by both variables being analyzed.
Regression to the mean describes extreme measurements becoming less extreme on repeat measurement and does not explain an induced exposure-outcome association after conditioning on referral.
key_expl: Specialty-clinic referral is a collider because both opioid use and severe pain increase the probability of referral. Restricting analysis to referred patients conditions on this common effect and can induce a spurious inverse association between its causes.
objective: Recognize collider bias when study inclusion or stratification conditions on a variable caused by both the exposure and the outcome.

system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
diagnosis: Use of teach-back to confirm patient understanding
mechanism: Teach-back is a nonshaming communication strategy in which the clinician asks the patient or caregiver to explain the plan or instructions in their own words. It tests the clarity of the clinician's explanation rather than the patient's intelligence or memory and allows immediate clarification and reteaching.
vignette: A 63-year-old woman is starting a new anticoagulant with a complex dosing schedule. After the clinician explains the plan, the patient nods and says that she understands. The clinician wants to confirm comprehension without embarrassing her.
correct: “I want to make sure I explained this clearly. Please tell me in your own words how you will take this medicine at home.”
distractors: “Do you understand the dosing schedule I just explained?”
“Please sign this form confirming that you understand the instructions.”
“Read the medication handout again after you get home.”
“I will ask your family to manage the medicine because the schedule is complicated.”
distractor_notes: A yes-or-no question does not reliably confirm comprehension; patients may answer yes despite misunderstanding.
A signature documents receipt or consent but does not demonstrate actual understanding of a medication plan.
Written materials can reinforce counseling but should not replace active confirmation of comprehension when the instructions are clinically important.
Automatically transferring responsibility to family undermines patient autonomy and is unnecessary without first assessing and supporting the patient's understanding.
key_expl: Teach-back asks the patient to explain the plan in their own words using nonshaming language. It directly verifies comprehension and allows the clinician to clarify and recheck any misunderstood information.
objective: Use the teach-back method to confirm patient understanding of complex medical instructions while preserving dignity and autonomy.
